ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS  
*201. [The questioner (Dr. Vijay Mallya) was absent. For answer vide . 
oage 27 infra]  
Loans to minorities on priority basis  
*202. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the RBI has written to Government that minorities will not get 
loans on priority basis, 
(b) the details of the RBI's objections and problems; 
(c) whether any alternative programme has been suggested by RBI to bring 
minorities within the settled-banking system; 
(d) if not, whether RBI and the banking system will avoid social priorities of 
Government; and 
(e) the steps proposed to evolve an alternative mechanism to ensure 
devolution of some powers from RBI? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to (e) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
Statement  
(a) to (e): As per instructions issued by the Gover nment of India, to ensure 
smooth flow of bank credit to minority communities, the RBI issued a master 
circular on 5th July, 2006 specifically on the issu e of credit facilities to 
minority communities. The circular directed the cre ation of Special Cells and 
designation of exclusive officers to be accountable and to be entrusted with the 
responsibility for ensuring publicity among minorit y communities of various 
programmes and suitable schemes for which bank credit can be made available. 
As per the circular, the lead banks in the identifi ed districts were required to 
involve the State Minority Commission/ Finance Corporation in the extension 
work to create awareness among and identification o f beneficiaries and 
preparation of viable projects. 
Subsequent to the release of the Prime Minister's r evised 15-Point 
Programme for the Welfare of Minorities, a further circular was issued by the 
Reserve Bank of India on 1st September, 2006. This circular brought to the 
notice of the banks that an important objective of the programme is to ensure that 
an appropriate percentage of priority sector lendin g is targeted for the minority 
communities. This circular has enjoined upon the banks to ensure that within the 
overall target for priority sector lending and the sub target of 10% for the weaker 
sections, sufficient care should be taken to ensure that the minority communities 
receive an equitable portion of the credit. With a view to ensure that the minority 
communities receive their due credit requirement, d iscussions are on with the 
Reserve Bank to ensure that more branches are opened in the minority concentration 
areas.

SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, two separate issues have arisen. One is the 
general issue as to what have we done in the last two-three years. End of March, 
2004, the total lending to minorities within the pr iority sector was Rs. 34,654 
crores. End of March, 2006, the amount was Rs. 45,490 crores. It is not correct 
to say that more loans are not being given to minor ities. I say that more loans 
are being given, but even more should be done. From Rs. 34,654 crores, we have 
come to Rs. 45,490 crores. This is the main question and I am answering what we 
have done in two years, but we should do more.

which the hon. Member has met me and I have explained it to him.

SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: I would like to put a specific  question. Who

Today, who are in majority in the rest of India, th ey are in minority in 
Kashmir. In Mizoram, they are in minority. In Nagaland, they are in minority. In

exact objections of the RBI and the IBA? You said that you have discussed this 
matter with the RBI and the IBA. What are the exact  objections of these two 
organisations? Finally, how much have you fixed as the loan amount? Is it Rs. 
25,000 or Rs. 50,000 or Rs. 1 lakh or Rs. 2 lakhs or Rs. 1 crore? What is the limit 
that you have fixed? 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, five communities have been notified by the 
Ministry of Welfare as minority communities. They are Sikhs, Muslims, Christians, 
Zorastrains and Buddhists. So, this is the definition of minority community.

DR. KARAN SINGH: Does that include Jammu and Kashmir?   
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: This goes by community, by religion. 
Now, Sir, as far as lending to priority sector is concerned, the Reserve Bank 
of India issues guidelines and circulars, from time  to time. On 5th July, 2006, 
the Reserve Bank issued instructions to banks with regard to providing credit 
facilities to minority communities. This is a Master Circular which incorporated 
all the guidelines issued, from time to time, colle cted at one place, which said 
that these guidelines must be followed by all the b anks while lending to the 
priority sector, with a special emphasis on credit to minority communities. 
Then, the Prime Minister's 15-Point Programme... 
SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Who mooted this idea? 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: I am answering. These guidelin es and 
circulars are issued, from time to time, over a per iod of years 
...(Interruptions)  
SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: No, no... 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: What is the point in saying, ' No, no'? I am

SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Mr. Finance Minister, don't misguide the House. I 
have put a specific supplementary. There was a Work ing Group which was 
working on that, and they have submitted a report. Please tell the House when 
this Working Group was formed and who mooted this idea. 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM. I am not able now to say wheth er a Working 
Group was appointed. I don't have that information.  These circulars and 
instructions issued, from time to time, over a peri od of years, were all 
captured in one circular, and this was issued on 5t h July, 2006. So, this 
considered all the circulars issued earlier and upd ated them. Then, came the 
Prime Minister's 15-Point Programme for the welfare of minorities.

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
When this 15-Point Programme was announced, the Reserve Bank issued another 
circular on 1st September, 2006, where they said th at within the priority sector 
lending, sufficient care should be taken to ensure that minority communities also 
receive an equitable part of the credit, and they g ave some guidelines as to 
how to go about doing that. Since then we are engag ed in discussions with 
the RBI and the IBA as to what changes should be made in the Master Circular 
and how this proportion of credit to minority communities can be enhanced. Sir, 
nobody has any objection, as such, to increasing credit to minority communities. 
There are points of view. These points of view have to be discussed and reconciled. 
As recently as February, we had a discussion; we are in communication with the 
RBI and the IBA, and i think, all these points of v iew can be reconciled and a 
policy decision can be evolved in the immediate future. At the moment, I can say 
with confidence that nobody has any objection. Vari ous aspects are being 
pointed out. All this has to be discussed, and a fi nal policy decision will be 
formulated, and the RBI will be advised to issue a circular in order to enhance the 
proportion of credit given to the minority community within the priority sector. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: How much time will it take? 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: I cannot fix a date. I will do my best to see that 
the RBI and the IBA are on board as far as possible. We will try to do it as early 
as possible. 
SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: What about your Committee? The y had 
constituted a Committee to look into it, and the Report is yet to come. 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, I am not aware of any Com mittee. I have 
instructed the Banking Division to have consultations with the IBA and the RBI. 
There is an exchange of letters. We have called them for discussion. If you are 
talking about the Committee, the only Committee I know of is the group which 
I am now closely monitoring.

SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, the Prime Minister's 15-point programme uses 
the expression appropriate percentage of private sector lending should be targeted for 
minority communities. On the basis of that, I answered the earlier question. There 
was a letter from the Principal Secretary to the Pr ime Minister which was 
addressed to the Division. It was not brought to my  notice. When the hon. 
Member, Mrs. Karat, wrote me the letter, I candidly  told her once I got the 
letter that I have obtained the file, and I found t here is such a letter On that 
letter, we are taking further action. 
I have discussed the matter with the Prime Minister . It is with the Prime 
Minister's consent that we are engaging IBA and RBI in discussion. I have kept 
the Prime Minister informed about the points of view of the IBA and the RBI. I 
have also told the Prime Minister that there are some aspects

which have to be discussed and reconciled, and once we discuss and reconcile 
these aspects with the RBI and the IBA, I shall rep ort back to the Prime 
Minister and whatever decision the Prime Minister t akes will, indeed, be 
implemented. 
It is unfortunate that, that letter was not brought to my notice between 24th 
November and 3rd January, and I candidly admitted to the hon. Member that that 
letter was no brought to my notice. And then, when she, I think, wrote to the 
Chairman, I explained my position that the letter was brought to my notice only 
on the 3rd of January. 
Since then, I have discussed the matter with the Prime Minister. The Prime 
Minister is fully informed of these discussions. On ce the discussions are 
completed, policy paper will be placed before the P rime Minister. Whatever 
decision the Prime Minister takes will, of course, be implemented.

SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD: Sir, I would like to invite the attention of 
the hon. Finance Minister to the second part of his reply, to be precise the sixth 
line of the second paragraph. It says, "This circular has enjoined upon the banks 
to ensure that within the overall target for priori ty sector lending and the sub-
target of 10 per cent for the weaker sections, sufficient care should be taken to 
ensure that the minority communities receive an equitable portion of the credit." 
What do you mean by the weaker sections? Which are the communities of people 
comprising the weaker sections? Do they include OBC s, the Most Backward 
Castes? I would like to know whether they include very poor people from the 
forward castes. 
Sir, the second part of my supplementary flows from the first. You talked about 
the view of the Reserve Bank of India which you con veyed to the hon. Prime 
Minister. Would you kindly share the view of the Reserve Bank with us as well as 
the whole House? What is the objection of the Reserve Bank of India and how 
are you going to reconcile that? 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, let me answer the first question first. The 
priority sector comprises of 15 categories. If you want me to read out the list, I 
can read it. It starts with agriculture, small-scal e industry, etc., and loans 
disbursed to urban poor. The weaker sections consist of nine categories and they 
are; (1) Small and marginal farmers with land holdings of 5 acres and less and 
landless labourers, tenant farmers and sharecropper s. (2) Artisans, village and 
cottage industries where individual credit limits do not exceed Rs. 50,000. (3) 
Beneficiaries of SGSY (4) Scheduled Castes and Sche duled Tribes. (5) 
Beneficiaries of differential growth of interest schemes. (6) Beneficiaries under 
the. Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana. (7) Beneficiaries under the scheme 
for liberation and rehabilitation of scavengers. (8) Advances to self-help groups. (9) 
Loans of distressed urban poor to repay their debt to non-institutional bankers. 
This constitutes weaker sections. The target for th e priority sector is 40 per 
cent of the total net bank credit. Within that 40 percentage points, 10 percentage 
points must go to the weaker sections. 
This has been the policy for many years. When we wa nt to lend to 
minorities, the RBI's view is that there may be som e double counting. I have 
taken a different view. That is why it is rather pr emature, Sir, to discuss the 
differences in approach; but, I am confident that t hese differences can be 
reconciled indiscussion. I have already advised the RBI that in our view 
11 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
there will be no double-counting in the user category, but we will resolve these 
things by discussion with the RBI. 
Secondly, RBI's view is that the correct approach s hould be to concentrate 
on districts where there is a heavy minority population. These districts have been 
identified; instructions have issued to the lead banks to prepare district credit 
plans to ensure that a large proportion of the dist rict plans are targeted towards 
the minorities. There are no differences of opinion . There are different 
perceptions and differences in approach. These perceptions and approaches will 
be reconciled and a policy will be laid down and th e policy will be 
implemented. 
MS. MABEL REBELLO: Sir, some of the minorities are also tribals, and 
they are marginal farmers. Last week we have discussed here that most of them

bound to sell it because they do not have the holdi ng capacity. Otherwise, they 
have to borrow money at an exorbitant rate of interest. I would like to know from 
the hon. Minister the quantum of money he has given to minority tribals in the 
central India. 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, I do not think I have tha t kind of a sub-
classification ...(Interruptions)... Sir, I do not have that kind of a classification. I will 
try to find out if among minorities the data captur es the minority tribals. If l 
am able to get that data. I will certainly send it to her.

Secretariat from the PMO to answer the hon. Ministe r. An inter-ministerial 
meeting was held by the Cabinet Secretariat where a ll the Secretaries were 
present how we could bring it at par. There are some problems, Sir. We, in the 
Archaeological Curvey, earn only about Rs. 53 crore from entry tickets, which is 
not at all enough for restoration, and conservation  work, which goes beyond 
Rs. 200 crores approximately. In any case, this Rs. 53 crores is put in the Central 
deposit fund of the Ministry of Finance and we have no access to it. That means 
that the Rs. 10 ticket is being subsidised by the Government of India. There is a 
debate going on in our Ministry whether it would be fair to subsidise even the entry 
fee for foreign nationals who are not taxpayers in our country. Sir, we have raised 
these points. Wherever we are charging extra fee from the foreigners, we are adding 
some value-added services. I have made a comparative study. The countries like 
the United States of America. Europe, the United Ki ngdom, etc. which have a 
single entry fee, these entry fees are very, very high, anything from 50 USD or 15 
Euros to 25 Euros or USD. If we were to increase th e fee for the Indian 
citizens travelling to various monuments of our country, in our personal opinion 
it would discourage the Indian travellers and we wa nt to encourage domestic 
tourism and if reduced further, which is already a minimal of Rs. 250 to world 
heritage site with value-added services. There are countries like Russia, Egypt 
and a lot of other developing countries. 
Reduction of entry fee in heritage monuments 
*203. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY: Will the Minister of CU LTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Prime Minister has asked the Ministry to 
14 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA   . 
evolve a mechanism to do away with the existing price of two tier entry fee in 
various heritage monuments for foreign and domestic tourists; and 
(b) if so, what measures are being taken by her Ministry to reduce the entry 
fee for the foreign tourists as compared to that of Indian tourists? 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRIMATI ABMIKA SONI): (a) and (b)A 
statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
(a) and (b) The existing policy of deferential char ges being levied for 
different services including entry fee in heritage monuments for foreign 
national was discussed in an Inter Ministerial Meeting, which was attended by the 
representatives of the Ministry of Culture. The Int er Ministerial Meeting 
recommended that the charges to foreigners and Indian citizens may be brought 
on par after obtaining necessary approvals. A final decision in the matter is not yet 
taken which have dual tariff. We are considering va rious other countries like 
SAARC and BIMSTEC but no final conclusions have been reached. This debate is 
going on in the Ministry. 
SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY: Sir, the hon. Minister while coming to this 
point has once again pointed out about the maintena nce of our world heritage 
sites and monuments. Sir, I am on the question of p romoting tourism in this 
country, especially for getting more foreign exchange and also to encourage the 
Indian tourists. Sir, I am not in favour of increasing the fee for Indian tourists on 
par with the foreign tourists. But what I want is that the foreign tourists should be 
brought on par with the Indian tourists so that a large number of tourists come here 
and they carry our culture to other countries. I think Rs. 50 crores is nothing as 
far as the Government of India is concerned. That is the point to which I would 
like to bring home. They should know our culture, out identity, our heritage, our 
architecture, and that is the point, which you have  to explain. Even the 
Government is spending hundreds of crores of rupees  on publicity in foreign 
countries. But they do not want to give concession to the foreign tourists who 
are coming. This is the point I would like to know. 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: Sir, we have written to the Ministry of Finance to 
create this fund which we earn from the ticket sale  as a non-lapsable fund for 
the Archaeological Survey of India so that we could  use this fund from ticket 
collection to restore the buildings. This has been supported by the Planning 
Commission. It rests with the Ministry of Finance. I am not at 
15 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
all of a different view with the Member that we want to encourage tourism I would 
like him to sit with me after the Question Hour and tell me in which country of the 
world do we get into monuments of world heritage status by paying such a paltry 
amount of Rs. 10/-. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Fix up some time. Fix up some time: 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: We are demeaning our monument s if we 
just allow Rs. 10/-, whereas for Indians, it is sti ll a big amount. We are even 
considering for senior citizens, students, special days so that they could even be 
given half this amount. But, for foreigners, if you want - this debate is going on -- 
you can give me your points, we can consider them as the debate progresses.

SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Sir, I would like to inform the hon. Minister 
that these tourist attractions are definitely good.  We expect tourists to come 
here, but, all over the world the tourist attractio n places are well maintained, 
and if the Government of India does not have enough funds, I do not think we 
should reduce it to a level where the maintenance of these tourist places become a 
problem, and these tourists, who are coming from all over the world, especially, 
from developed world, I do not think the rates which the Government of India or 
the Department is charging, are so high. On the other hand, I would like to know 
from the hon. Minister what kind of subsidy the Government of India is giving for 
this. Supposing, they 
16 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
are already giving crores of rupees for subsidies, how do we like to manage these 
heritage sites so that they are well maintained for  hundreds and thousands of 
years more or they well be dilapidated. It is easy to say, 'reduce the rates'. But 
then, the Finance Minister, who is sitting here wil l tax all of us, who are not 
visiting that place. So, only those who are willing to visit have to pay for that 
kind of maintenance. 
SHRIMATI  AMBIKA SONI: It is a fact that increasingly numbers  are 
going up of monuments which are preserved and conse rved by the 
Archaeological Survey and by State Government's Arc haeological 
Department. It is a matter of satisfaction that in the recent Budget the Finance 
Minister did marginally increase the Budgetary outl ay of the Archaeological 
Survey. Sir, we have tried to involve public-private partnership in the preservation of 
monuments because there is no other way of doing this work. So we have started a 
National Cultural Fund where the Ministry of Finance has offered to give tax 
rebates and incentives to those who contribute sums  for the preservation of 
monuments. To make it easier for corporate houses to preserve monuments, we 
have asked them to bring their own expertise and conservationists only under our 
overall supervision. 
But, I am very sorry to say, the response is still not adequate and need more 
resources than what we have to maintain our monuments. Every hon. Member 
of Parliament wants some monument in his or her con stituency to be looked 
after by the ASI. We have 3,776 monuments under the ASI. But, this is a very 
insignificant number considering the large amount of heritage which we need 
to conserve. 
SHRI B.J. PANDA: Sir, would the hon. Minister clari fy whether she is 
aware of many-incidents, which have been reported in the media, of India citizens 
being harassed at these monuments, particularly Indian citizens from the North-
East, on the ground that they might be foreigners? Also, it has been reported that 
often times people who don't hold the lndian Passport but are somewhat Indian-
looking are not harassed. Now, is there any guideline that the Ministry issued, 
or is it left to the discretion of the gatekeepers?  And, will she take steps to 
ensure that Indian citizens are not harassed at these monuments? 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: Sir, it is our constant effor t and it is an on-
going process. If it needs to be strengthened, we will strengthen that no indian 
citizen, or, for that matter, no visitor, is harassed at any of the 
17 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
monuments he visit in India. Without any doubt in m y mind, if there are some 
lacunae, some loophole, we will plug them. I have n ot heard of the incident 
which the hon. Member is talking about. I will find out. But, it is true that there 
are people who have an Indian appearance: They can be, sometimes, thought of 
as Indian citizens and pay a smaller fee. Sir, only  yesterday/while 1 was 
preparing for this question, this matter came up th at a citizen who was from our 
neighbouring country and looks like one of our people, was charged only Rs. 10. 
And, subsequently, when he started speaking and had a different accent, he was 
called back and asked to show his identification. W hen he could not show an 
Indian card, he had to pay Rs. 250. 
SHRI B.J. PANDA: Indians are repeatedly harassed. Please look into it. 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: I will certainly look into it.

Now, Sir, when one travels across the world, you have to pay 10— 15 dollars to 
get in anywhere in the world.. Why should an American citizen, for example,

the transmission tariff for customers in Gujarat ge tting gas through regional 
networks is lower.

Co-ordination between customs and licencing authority  
*218.DR. K. MALAISAMY; 
SHRI S.ANBALAGAN: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) what is the mechanism to co-ordinate between custom s authority and 
licencing authority; 
(b) whether it has been adequate and effective, and if not, what are the 
measures in the offing; 
(c) whether there is any co-ordination mechanism and reconciliation process 
among assessment group/SVB/SIIB in the assessment of value and levying of 
customs duty; 
(d) what is the machinery to monitor the observation given by SMS; and 
(e) whether there are cases of non-fulfilment of Export  Obligation due to 
incorrect reckoning of export and if so, what are t he measures to check the 
recurrence of this type of lapses? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) and (b) 
There is a well laid-down coordination mechanism between the customs and the 
licensing authorities. At the Ministry level, the D epartment of Revenue is 
represented in the various Committees of Department  of Commerce and 
DGFT, like the Board of Approval, Norms Committee, DEPB 
46

Committee, Grievance Redressal Committee etc, which  facilitate proper 
coordination between the two Departments. Trade Fac ilitation Committee 
meetings provide a forum for exchange of views between the customs and the 
licensing authorities at regional levels. The exist ing coordination mechanism 
is considered to be adequate and effective. The coordination mechanism will be 
improved further after the Electronic Data Interchange between the customs and 
the licensing authorities is fully established for all export promotion schemes. 
(c) and (d) The Special Valuation Branch (SVB), Spe cial Intelligence and 
Investigation Branch (SIIB) and Appraising Groups work in close coordination 
with one another to safeguard Government revenue. The SVBs provide valuable 
inputs to the asessing officers for valuation of the goods. The SIIB issues Alerts, 
Modus Operandi Circulars from time to time which provide valuable guidance to 
the assessing officers. References made by the Appraising Groups to SVB/SIIB are 
monitored by the supervisory officers in the Custom Houses.

reasons. However, no cases of non-fulfilment of exp ort obligation due to the 
alleged incorrect reckoning of export have been reported.

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
Mineral water and soft drink bottling plants 
*220. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Will the Minister o f WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of mineral water and soft drink bo ttling plants 
operating in the country, State-wise; 
(b) how many of the above have been permitted by the Central Ground Water 
Board or any other competent authority of either Central or State Government; 
(c) the volume of ground water extracted by them, during the last three years, 
and whether it is free of cost; 
(d) what measures are being adopted to stop over utilis ation of water 
reserves; and 
(e) whether his Ministry is contemplating to fix rates of water, in view of its 
commercial utilization? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) As per the 
data available with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the number of 
companies (Licenses) manufacturing and selling ISI marked Packaged 
Drinking Water (PDW) as per IS 14543:2004 and miner al water as per 
13428:2004 are 1439 and 9 respectively. The State-w ise details are given in 
Statement-I (See below). 
(b) Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) constituted u nder the 
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 regulates ground water extraction by new 
industries proposed to be set up in over-exploited/ critical areas by giving 
clearance on case to case basis. The CGWA has accor ded permission to 10 
packaged drinking water units since 2003. State-wise information is given in 
Statement-ll (See below). 
(c) 'Water' being a State subject, the licensing author ities in the States like 
State Pollution Control Bords/Village Panchayats etc. fix the quantum of ground 
water extraction for industry including mineral water/soft drink bottling plants. 
Information as received from various State/UT Governments regarding withdrawal 
of ground water and charges, if any, being levied by them is given in Statement-
Ill (See below). 
62 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(d) and (e) 'Water' being a State subject, necessar y measures to stop over-
utilization of ground water and to fix rates for commercial exploitation of ground 
water is to be taken by the States. However, Union Government has undertaken the 
following measures to check over-exploitation of ground water.— 
(i) Notification of 43 Over-exploited areas in the country for regulation of 
ground water development and management. In these n otified areas, 
installation of new ground water abstraction structures is not permitted 
without prior specific approval of the Authority. 
(ii) Notification of 65 Over-exploited areas in var ious States, which 
showed a very steep decline in ground water levels and required action 
for regulation for registration of ground water abstraction structures. 
(iii) Issuance of directions to Group Housing Socie ties, Institutes, 
Hotels, Industries, Farm Houses, etc. in the notifi ed areas of Delhi, 
Faridabad, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad and other areas of  NCT Delhi 
where ground water table is below 8 metres from ground surface, to adopt 
rain water harvesting system. 
(iv) Issuance of directions to the Chief Secretaries of the concerned States 
to take all measures to adopt artificial recharge to ground water/promote 
rain water harvesting in all the Over-exploited areas falling under their 
jurisdiction and ensure inclusion of roof top rain water harvesting in 
the building bye-laws. 
(v) Central Ground Water Authority is regulating wi thdrawal of ground 
water by industries/projects in over-exploited and critical areas. List of 
these areas has been circulated to the State Pollut ion Control Boards 
and Ministry of Environment & Forests which refer t he new or 
expansion of industries/projects to CGWA for obtain ing permission. 
The proposals are evaluated on case-to-case basis o n site specific 
technical studies/recommendations from Regional Offices of CGWB. 
One of the pre-conditions of the permissions is mandatory adoption of 
rain water harvesting. 
 Besides the above, Ministry of Water Resources have circulated a Model Bill to 
regulate and control the development and management of ground water to the 
States/Union Territories to enable them to enact su itable ground water 
legislation. The States of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Him achal Pradesh, Kerala, 
Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Union Territories of La kshadweep and 
Pondicherry have enacted ground water legislation.

1564. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of FIN ANCE be

shareholders? " 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (S HRI 
PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL): (a) to (c) No, Sir. In view of the special nature of 
banks and the importance of ensuring that significant shareholders of a banking 
company are "fit and proper" persons, the Government introduced the Banking 
Regulation (Amendment) Bill, 2005 in Lok Sabha on 13th May, 2005. The Bill 
inter alia provides to remove the restrictions on voting rights concurrently with 
the stipulation of statutory requirement of prior a pproval for acquisition of 
shares above the specified limit. A new section 12(B) is being inserted to provide

acquisition of shares of the banking company is by a person considered "fit and 
proper". The rationale for removing cap on voting rights is to give shareholders a 
right to vote, which is commensurate with the equity capital held by them.

1579. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKER REDDY: Will the Minister of 
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:   ' 
(a) whether it is a fact that the difference in price b etween subsidized and

(c) whether Government are according top priority to pr eventing 
aduIteration of petroleum products; 
(d) if so, the steps taken in this regard during the last three years; and 
(e) the number of cases filed and disposed off during the last three years? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PATEL): (a) to (d) The possibility of 
adulteration of petrol/diesel by some unscrupulous elements cannot be ruled 
out due to huge price difference between petrol/diesel and various adulterants 
including Kerosene available in the market and the easy miscibility of these 
products with petrol/diesel. To check adulteration in auto fuels and diversion 
of PDS Kerosene, Government has asked Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to 
take various steps to contain the menace of adulteration:— 
(i) Under the Control Orders issued by the Governme nt to prevent fuel 
adulteration, under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, State 
Governments are empowered to take action against those indulging in 
adulteration. Government have requested the State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations to take  steps to 
control adulteration. 
(ii) OMCs undertake regular and surprise inspection s of Retail Outlets 
and also take action under Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) and 
Dealership Agreements against those indulging in 
156 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
adulteration and malpractices. MDG provide for termination of 
dealership in cases of adulteration being established. 
(iii) Government has taken the initiative to expedi te the installation of 
Global Positioning System (GPS) to monitor the move ment of tank 
trucks. 
(iv) OMCs have introduced new tamper proof tank-tru ck locking 
systems to prevent en-route adulteration by transporters. 
(v) Keeping in view the misuse/diversion of SKO for  adulteration, the 
import of SKO by private parties has been canalized through OMCs. 
(vi) As advised by the Government, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have 
created a separate wing to report to a Director oth er than Director 
(Marketing), which will oversee and monitor all act ivities and 
operations to curb adulteration and specify norms a nd guidelines in 
this regard. 
In order to check adulteration the Government had r ecently taken a 
number of new initiatives which are given in the Statement-I (See below). 
(e) The details of inspections conducted by OMCs an d action taken on 
defaulting dealers on account of various malpractices during the last three years 
are given in Statement-ll. 
Statement -I 
Details of new initiatives taken to check adulteration of  
Petrol/Diesel and streamlining PDS kerosene  
'distribution  
Checking adulteration is a continuous process and t he Ministry of 
Petroleum and Natural Gas has been reviewing steps taken to curb 
adulteration from time to time. In the process, sev eral technological and 
institutional measures have been taken to contain adulteration. The recent steps 
taken by the Ministry are summarized below: 
1. Automation of Retail Outlets: In order to monito r the activities at retail 
outlets by adopting the latest technological improv ements, adutomation of 
retail outlets is being implemented. MOP&NG has directed 
157 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
the oil marketing companies to complete automation of retail outlets selling more 
than 200 per month by March, 2007. 
2. Third Party Certification of Retail Outlets: OMCs have been directed to 
complete third party certification of all the retail outlets selling more than 100 
KL per month by March, 2007. 
3. Monitoring of movement of Tank Trucks through Globa l Positioning 
System (GPS): In order to prevent adulteration duri ng transportation, OMCs 
have been directed to install GPS for complete moni toring of the movement 
of all the company owned/dealer owned/ contractor o wned tanks trucks by 
March, 2007. 
4. Marker System in Kerosene: To check adulteration in  auto fuels, 
Government has asked public sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to take 
various steps, including introduction of marker in adulterants. OMCs have 
commenced introduction of marker in kerosene on all  India basis with effect 
from 1.10.2006. Under the new system, Marker is being put in kerosene in all 
depots. This system heralds the introduction of wor ld class technology to 
curb and eventually eliminate the menace of adulter ation of transportation 
fuels along the supply chain. With the marker's presence, adulteration even with 
very low levels of kerosene can be detected. 
MS/HSD Control Order, 2005, SKO Control Order, 1993 and MDG 2005 have 
been amended for making provision regarding introduction of marker system in 
Kerosene to check adulteration. A committee has been set up in the Ministry to 
monitor the progress of the marker system. Oil Mark eting Companies in the 
Private sector have also been simultaneously asked to introduce marker in 
Kerosene as is being done by Public Sector OMCs. 
5. Revising the Marketing Discipline Guidelines: The M arketing 
Discipline Guidelines (MDG) under which the oil mar keting companies take 
penal actions against the erring dealers have been revised during August, 2005 
making the penal action more stringent. As per MDG, 2005, a dealership would 
be terminated in the first instance of adulteration itself. 
6. Jan Kerosene Pariyojana: To streamline the PDS Kero sene distribution 
system and contain diversion of kerosene for adulteration and other unauthorized 
usages, Jan Kerosene Pariyojana (JKP) had been laun ched initially for a 
period of 6 months on a pilot basis in 414 blocks w ith effect from 2.10.2005. 
The Pilot scheme has been further extended upto 30.6.2007. 
158 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
7. Smart Card Scheme: With the objective of ensuring that the benefit of the 
subsidy reaches the targeted consumers in an effici ent and cost-effective 
manner and to prevent any leakages, this Ministry has proposed introduction of Smart 
Card System for distribution of PDS kerosene. The s cheme is proposed to be 
introduced initially on an experimental basis. In t he Pilot project, subsidized 
kerosene through Smart Card is proposed to be available to BPL families while 
all other ration card holders would be given non-su bsidized kerosene. Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs) would ensure adequate availability of PDS as 
well as non-subsidized kerosene during the entire period of implementation of 
the Pilot.

The production of oil depends on the potential of t he producing field and

Interlinking of rivers  
1618. SHRI K.P.K. KUMARAN: Will the Minister of WAT ER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) what are the latest developments in the matter of inter-linking Indian rivers 
in general and the peninsula rivers in particular; and 
(b) whether while addressing a Press Conference at Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu 
recently he had said that matters are moving at a natural pace and the farmers of 
Tamil Nadu are at their wits end to give any concrete shape to this abstract phrase 
and whether he propose to offer a clarification so that these farmers may find a 
ray of hope? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) The Ministry of 
Water Resources (MOWR) (erstwhile Ministry of Irrigation) and Central Water 
Commission (CWC) formulated a National Perspective Plan (NPP) for Water 
Resources Development in 1980 envisaging inter-basin transfer of water from 
surplus basins to deficit basins/areas which compri ses of two components, 
namely, Himalayan Rivers Development Component and Peninsular Rivers 
Development Component. National Water Development Agency (NWDA) was 
set up under the MOWR in 1982 for carrying out vari ous technical studies to 
establish the feasibility of the proposals of NPP and to give concerete shape to it. 
Based on various studies conducted, NWDA has identified 30 links (16 under 
Peninsular Component & 14 under Himalayan Component) for the preparation 
of Feasibility Reports (FRs). Out of these, FRs of 14 links under Peninsular 
Component and 2 links (Indian Portion) under Himala yan Component have 
already been completed. Further, a Memorandum of Un derstanding for the 
preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) of one of the links in Peninsular 
Component Namely Ken-Betwa link was signed among th e Central 
Government and State Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh 
209 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
on 25th August, 2005. Subsequently, the Central Gov ernment entrusted the 
preparation of the DPR of the aforesaid link to NWDA, which is planned to be 
completed by June, 2008. 
(b) As per the relevant information published in the media (dated 8.2.07), the 
Hon'ble Minister stated that work on inter-linking of rivers was proceeding at "natural 
pace" and was not slow, as it was being perceived. Further, he stated that the 
Ministry was not bound by any time frame as the entire process of arriving at a 
decision involved a period of consultation with and consensus of the States that 
were concerned in the matter.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (c) As per 
information provided by the Ministry of Urban Development, shortage of water 
for drinking purposes is not anticipated in near future. With a view to provide safe 
drinking water supply to urban population, the Ministry of Urban Development 
has initiated a reforms linked programme called Jaw aharlal Nehru National 
Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) under which additional central assistance is 
made available to 63 selected cities including mega /metro cities, state capitals 
and other important cities for the development of integrated urban infrastructure 
including those for water supply. A similar program me called Urban 
Infrastructure Development Scheme for Small and Medium Town (UIDSSMT) 
has also been launched by the Ministry of Urban Dev elopment along with 
JNNURM, for the improvement of drinking water suppl y in 5098 small and 
medium towns and cities (as per census 2001) not co vered under JNNURM. 
Both the programmes viz. JNNURM & UIDSSMT are being implemented in a 
mission mode during the seven year period from 2005-06 to 2012-13. 
In view of the declining ground water levels in som e areas, necessary 
measures have been taken by the State Governments a nd Central Government 
which include rainwater harvesting and artificial recharge. The Government of India 
has also drafted a "Model Bill to Regulate and Cont rol the Development and 
Management of Ground Water" and circulated to all

The Finance Minister in his budget Speech 2007-08 has announced a scheme

SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI (Kerala): Sir, some of my colleagues have already 
spoken on this subject highlighting certain vital areas. Normally, when the Railway 
Budget is announced, the common man's anxiety is centred around three areas. All those 
aspects have been very well taken care of by the Railway Minister in this Budget. These 
are rail fare, freight charges and new trains. In the area of rail fare, there is, actually, a 
reduction, and this is an appreciable measure. But while evaluating the entire text of 
Budget, one thing is certain. The serious aspect of  safety has been heavily 
compromised. So, firstly, adequate allocation is not there. And there is no meticulous 
plan which has been 
274 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
envisaged. I want to specifically refer to certain areas. The Parliamentary 
Standing Committee on Railways, after its evaluation regarding railway bridges, 
made a suggestion. Altogether the Railways have mor e than 1 lakh railway 
bridges, and amongst them, that is, nearly 50,000 bridges were built during the 
British period. Our Standing Committee suggested urgent reconstruction of 300 
bridges. But, in the Budget, there is no serious ef fort to undertake that 
responsibility on a war-footing basis, within a tim e schedule. That is one point 
which I want to refer for the consideration of the Railway Minister. Another thing 
is that nearly 18,000 kms. stretch of track is to be renewed urgently. 
That is a task that involves big money. But the poi nt is, the safety aspect, 
the renewal of this entire 18,000 kilometres of track is very much necessary. 
Further, we all know that unmanned crossings are hi ghly accident-prone. 
We have thousands and thousands of such unmanned crossings in the country. 
A proper approach must be evolved in this respect. This aspect has to be taken 
care of. 
Another point that I wish to mention about the safe ty aspect relates to our 
loco-pilots who run the trains. There are nearly 40,000 plus of them in the country. 
They are the backbone of the railway workforce. They have been facing a very 
serious problem. This problem has been there with us for a very long time. We 
have been discussing this for many, many years now. The issue is that this vital 
workforce has not been enjoying the international 8 -hour duty norm. Our 
Parliamentary Standing Committee, under the chairma nship of Shri Basudeb 
Acharia, had, recently, suggested the adoption of this eight-hour duty norm for our 
loco-pilots. I request the hon. Minister to give an assurance in this regard while 
replying to the debate. We have to redress this very genuine demand of our loco-
pilots. We must ensure them the eight-hour duty fac ility. I am emphasising on 
this because it is very much related to safety in the running of our railways. The 
Railways are now in profit. There is no need of con tinuing with any restriction 
on the recruitment of people. Already there are so many vacancies in the 
Railways. In the Railway Protection Force only, 8000 vacancies exist. It is there 
in the Budget. So, on this issue pertaining to the loco-pilots, instead of this 12 to 
14 hour duty, or even extended duty hours that we a re practising now, let us 
adopt the eight-hour duty norm 
275 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
and recruit more and more pilots so that we can assure the country that we are 
really serious about safety in the running of our R ailways. I am stressing on 
this point and I am also requesting the Minister to  give an assurance while 
replying to the debate. 
Another matter is the assessment of our total requi rement of coaches and 
wagons. There has been no proper projection of this  future requirement. This 
needs to be considered. In this Budget, one wagon f actory has been 
announced to be set up in Kerala. That is a welcome  step. We are happy with 
that. But the things like the capacity of the unit, the number of wagons that are 
going to be manufactured etc. need to be assessed and calculated on the basis 
of the total estimated requirement of wagons in the coming years. There has to 
be a correct picture of the requirement in the coming years. While saying that, I 
want to make one more point. What is the real safet y-audit-certification record 
available in respect of our coaches and engines? So me of them are very old. 
Some of them have become totally obsolete. These ar e to be replaced. So, 
replacement is an issue. We should calculate our fu ture requirement in a very 
comprehensive manner. 
[THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA) in the Chair] 
Another aspect of the Budget which has been a disturbing one is that of Public-
Private Partnership. Sir, we all know that, already, certain activities in Railways are 
being outsourced. Reservation and ticketing is outsourced. Catering is outsourced. 
Even the Retiring Rooms and the Yatri Niwas .mainte nance is outsourced. 
With this continued outsourcing and privatisation, where are we leading our 
country to? What has been our experience and the in ternational experience, 
including Britain's experience, of privatisation of railways? We should be doubly 
cautious while moving on this path of privatisation . We are opposed to it. Our 
party is totally opposed to it for the sake of the safety of our passengers and the 
efficient running of our railways. The public sector is not inefficient. Nobody can 
say that. It is the public sector is which we can e nsure accountability. Then, 
while speaking in the House, the hon. Minister referred to the issue of privatisation. 
Personally, he is not for privatisation. The hon. M inister's ■personal position is 
good. But, what is going to happen generally? The economy is now taking such a 
privatisation course which will give negative results. That is why we are firmly saying 
that privatisation efforts in Railways should be firmly stopped. It should be stopped 
drastically. 
276 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
1 00 PM 
Sir, another issue I want to raise is relating to t wo lowest group of workers 
in the Railways. One is the catering staff. Now, th e catering is with the private 
people. Privatisation is the order of the day now. We agree. But, the point is, while 
you give a new contract, the workers of the catering service should continue in the 
new contract also. They should also be given adequa te pay No assurance has 
been given by the hon. Minister in his Budget on this issue. As far as the licensed 
porters in Railways are concerned, they are not get ting the wages which they 
used to get earlier. More so. their jobs are being taken away by Private parties. In 
his initial Budget, Laluji gave so many assurances and made so many promises to 
the porters The porters celebrated that But, finally, these people are losing their 
jobs even at stations. So, my request is, that issu e should be revisited, and an 
assurance should be given that the porters would get job security and income 
security. 
Finally, Sir, I request you to allow me to raise two-three points pertaining to the 
State of Kerala. Firstly, yesterday, we saw some developments in this House Sir, 
first of all, let me say that we are not against formation of Salem Division. While 
talking about bifurcation of the division, our Memb ers from Tamil Nadu are 
having the impression that we are opposing formation of Salem Division. No, we 
are not opposing that. The Salem Division can be fo rmed. But, while forming a 
new Division, certain criteria, norms and conventio ns are practised by the 
Railways hitherto. It should be followed. The bifurcation is being done in such a 
way that Palakkad is given a small area and the big ger area is being given to 
Salem. The mother unit is smaller and the newborn c hild unit is becoming 
bigger  (Interruptions). .  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA) You have to finish 
now. You have already taken much longer than the time allotted to you 
277 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Sir, I will conclude within two minutes. On that 
question, Laluji rightly referred that matter for c onsultation with the respective 
Chief Ministers of both the States. We agree with t hat position. But, what is 
happening in the ground is, the statements made by the Minister of State in the 
Ministry of Railways, Shri Veluji are not fair for an MOS. That much only I am 
saying. Now, I am using an additional word 'unfair' . So, that is to be looked 
into. 
Sir, another question is, the hon. Members of Parliament from Kerala met the 
hon. Prime Minister to demand the formation of a ne w zone, namely, West 
Coast Zone. As per our understanding, such a zone i s required to take care of 
the aspirations of the people of that area. The hon. Prime Minister asked us to give 
a memorandum on this issue. Now, while referring to this issue, I want to say 
that the Railway Ministry and the Planning Commissi on should look into this 
issue to know the potential and possibility of forming a new zone so that it takes 
care of all the districts in that area. Sir, anothe r point is 
regarding. ..(Interruptions)...  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA): No more another thing 
please. The time is over. 
SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Sir, electrification in th e Malabar area is 
neglected in the Budget. 
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA): They will do it. Don't 
worry. 
SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Sir, the question of doubling of the entire stretch 
of the railway line in Kerala is to be taken on a war-footing. 
Sir, another issue is, the International Container Transhipment Terminal is 
coming up at Kochi, Vallarpadam; everybody knows it. We are going to take up 
that responsibility. We have to cater to the requirements of that project. Edapalli 
to Guruvayur and Guruvayur to Thannur railway line is to 
278 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
be taken up immediately. It has not been properly included in the Railway Budget. 
Sir, with these words I conclude. Thank you, Sir. 
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA):As per the order, there is 
no lunch hour today. So, we will continue the discussion. Shri Abu Asim Azim. 
You have got 13 minutes.

SHRI P.J. KURIEN (Kerala): Sir, I will take only a few minutes. The 
Railways is just a unifying factor and I find that the Railways have become the 
cause for division. .I think the discussion on the basis of Bihari or 
Maharashtrian or State-wise or otherwise should not  have happened on the 
Railway Budget. 
[MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair]  
Sir, with regard to this Budget, I would like to sa y that this is one of the 
best Budgets that this House has ever seen. This is  the Railway Minister's 
fourth consecutive Budget and there has been no hike in the passenger fares in 
all the four Budgets. I think this is a miracle. It is said that the Minister does not 
have any magic wand. But I find as if he has a magic wand. Otherwise, how can 
he achieve it much without any hike in fares? The Railways which is said to be 
a white elephant has turned around and become a pro fitable concern. There 
is no passenger fare hike; there is reduction in fr eight charges for cement, 
petrol, etc.; there are 40 new trains; there is 50 per cent concession for 
students; there is special consideration for disabled persons and women above 
45 years. Well, a very people friendly Budget has b een appreciated by both 
sides. It is getting bouquets and accolades from both sides. I must congratulate 
the Railway Minister. Shri Manohar Joshi was suppor ting and praising the 
Minister. I think many on the other side who are re alistic, are all supporting 
this budget. The Railway Minister deserves compliments and I congratulate him. 
I don't want to dwell more on that. I come to my St ate, Kerala. Unfortunately, 
Laluji left the House when I started speaking. I hope Shri Velu would convey my 
request to him. The first thing is that for Kerala, we are asking for a West Coast 
Railway Zone. We have the Palakkad Division, we have the Trivandrum Division. 
The Palakkad Division and the Trivandrum Division comprise areas from three 
States, that is, Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. So taking these two 
divisions, and the new Salem Division, a new Railwa y Zone can be created 
with Trivandrum as its Headquarters, which can be called West Coast Railway 
Zone. After all a number of new zones have been cre ated. This Government 
also created a new railway zone earlier. Sir, this is a demand of the people of 
Kerala and is pending for long time. All Governments, 
3.13 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
whether the Left Front Government, or the UDF Government and all MPs have 
made this demand. I request the Railway Minister to consider this demand very 
seriously. I am requesting both Shri Velu and Shri Laluji to consider it 
personally. It is not a very expensive proposal. I am happy that Shri Velu is 
taking note of it. There is a misunderstanding that  we Keralites are opposing 
the Salem Division. Yes, you have created a new Salem Division. That is okay. 
We do not grudge it. But when you create a new divi sion, there are certain 
norms and guidelines to be adhered to. What has hap pened is, the new 
division has been created from the Palakkad Divisio n by taking away the 
major portion of the Palakkad Division. That is unf air and unjust. Now after the 
new division is created, the new Salem Division has  become bigger and the 
Palakkad Division has become smaller. Somebody was saying an analogy 
'the child is bigger than the mother'. This is unfa ir and unjust. We want justice. 
When a new division is created, what you should do is, take areas from all 
surrounding divisions. You take some portion from the Palakkad Division, some 
portion from Madurai and some from Trichy and whichever is the other division 
and then form a new Salem Division. To think that the new division should have 
all Tamil Nadu region of Palakkad Division and the new division should certainly 
be bigger than the mother division, that thinking s macks of parochialism and 
narrow-mindedness, the Minister should not have that kind of thinking. That is 
what I have to say. ...(Interruptions)... Sir, I can yield, but you should give that 
time to me. I am yielding. 
SHRI B.S. GNANADESIKAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, as the name of the Minister 
has been drawn here. I would like to clarify it. We  are not pro-Salem or anti-
Salem. With reference to the facts which my learned colleague has mentioned, so far 
as Kerala is concerned, the total earning is, would be Rs. 265 crores, minus the 
Salem Division. In Tamil Nadu, it would be Rs. 200 crores if the Salem Division 
is created. So far as the revenue aspect is concern ed, Kerala is earning 
more. 
PROF. P.J. KURIEN: You cannot reply to me. ...(Interruptions)....  
SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY: If they want, let them take whatever they want to 
take. But let them not blame somebody or any other State. Don't bring 
regionalism in the Railways. That is what I want to say ...(Interruptions)...  
PROF. P.J. KURIEN: That is exactly what I said, (Interruptions)  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Mr. Narayanasamy, please ...(interruptions)...  
PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Sir, Mr. Narayanasamy is saying the same thing that I 
have said. I said that a new division should not be on the basis of 
314 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
State or region and should not be parochial. You take it from everywhere. I only 
said that. I agree with Shri Narayanasamy. He is my  good friend. Further, I 
support the Salem Division. I am not against the Salem Division. It should be there. 
It should be there. I have no complaints about that. But what I say is that it should 
not be formed by taking a major portion of the Palakkad Division, that is what I 
am saying... 
SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY: Don't bring in Minister's name. 
PROF. P.J. KURIEN: The Minister's name will come. Y ou become a 
Minister and I will use your name also. But what ca n I do? You are not a 
Minister. Sir, another thing which I would like to mention is ...............  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS ( SHRI R. 
VELU): I would like to say something here because earlier also one of the hon. 
Members said that the Minister was unfair. Now, my very good friend said that a 
parochial attitude has been adopted. As a point of clarification, I want to mention 
that this Division was not created overnight. A Special Officer was appointed. He 
went into the entire matter in detail and considered all aspects like which places 
to be covered, the possible viability, further growth, etc. It took one full years for him 
to take a decision, and this was then put up before  the Railway Board. Then, 
every wing of the Railway Board went into this matt er. Transport, engineering 
and all other related department went into the issue, and ultimately recommended 
setting up of this Division. As my friends have men tioned, we have not taken 
the entire Palakkad Division in this route. There i s the Madukkarai cement 
factory which gives an earning of Rs. 7.72 crores, and this has been given to 
the Palakkad Division. If you look at it transactio n-wise, earning-wise and 
employees-wise, which come to 8,800 and 8,200, the difference is very less. 
Further, the Valliyar cement factory, Madurai cemen t factory and the 
Mangalore port are going to yield a lot of income b ecause Hassan-Mangalore 
line is going to become operational. Iron exports w ould also give income. So 
viability is not questionable; number of employees is also not questionable. No 
office is going to be closed down. ...(Interruptions)....  
THE MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS (SHRI VAYALAR RAVI): 
Members from Karnataka should not get provoked. 
315 

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Nobody from Karnataka is prese nt here to get 
provoked. And, I am sitting here. 
SHRI R. VELU: Also, out of 1,130 kms., the Salem Division has got around 
600 kms. and the Palakkad Division has got only 57 kms. less than the Salem 
Division. After all this difference of 57 kms. does  not matter. In India, there are 
10 Divisions which are either less than that or which are of the same length. To 
be precise, six of them are less than 500 kms. and four of them are around 
500 kms. So, viability is not questionable. The rou te is not questionable. The 
number of employees also is not questionable and, n o offices have been 
closed down. Then, what is the problem? 
PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Sir, I am not for any argument with the hon. Minister. However, 
I am happy that he has admitted that the new Division, that has been formed, that 
is the Salem Division, is length-wise bigger than the Palakkad Division, The new 
one, Salem Division, has 600 plus kms., while the old one, Palakkad Division, has 
500 plus kms. that is my only complaint which he has admitted. All other things are 
okay. When a division is formed from an existing one, how can the new one be 
bigger than the existing one? That is what I say is  unfair. If the Minister is hurt 
by my statement, then, I am ready to withdraw it. B ut fact is a fact and he has 
admitted that ...(Interruptions)... I am not yielding. 
DR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Mr. Kurien, you please proceed to the next point. 
This has been explained in detail by the hon. Minister. 
PROF. P.J. KURIEN: I move on to my next point. Now, the hon. Minister, Lalu 
Prasad Yadavji, called all the MPs and gave us an assurance that the matter would 
be discussed with the two Chief Ministers and sorted out.! am requesting that that 
assurance, that he will call both the Chief Ministers and the dispute will be sorted 
out, should be fulfilled. 
The next point that I wish to make is very, very important. In fact, the reason 
why I got up to speak today is mainly this. 
Sir, I want your personal indulgence in the matter. My time was taken away 
by the Minister and Mr. Narayanasamy, who is the Chief Whip and who should 
actually protect me; but he is not doing that. Sir, today, some people came to my 
house in the morning. Some of them were blind, some were handicapped; some 
were deaf. They gave me a representation. Do 
316 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
you know what it was? I am sure, the other MPs must  have also known about 
it. Now, at railway stations there are telephone booths. In 1981, Indiraji, the then 
Prime Minister, decided at that time, that telephone booths at railway stations will be 
manned by handicapped, physically disabled and ment ally challenged people. 
So, they were given these booths. If you go to any railway station you can see either 
a deaf or a blind or a physically handicapped person operating the booth. What 
happened now? The Railway Board took a decision. I can't believe that a Minister 
like Shri Lalu Prasad Yadav, he, one who introduced the garib raths in the country, 
would have agreed to that. I think this has been do ne by the Railway Board 
without the knowledge of the Minister. I refuse to believe that Lalu Prasad Yadav 
can do this. All these physically handicapped, deaf and blind people have been told 
to pack up and go. Their booths are being taken away and those booths are going to 
be given to multi-nationals or, I don't know, to whom. It is said that this decision 
was taken in April, 2005. After they complained against this decision, they were 
given extension up to April, 2007. Now, they have all been asked to get out of 
railway stations because these booths are going to be given to some other 
people. I do not want to say anything more. Sir, let me tell you, if that happens I will 
sit here on dhama, on fast. (Interruptions) Yes. I will sit here on dhama.  
SOME HON. MEMBERS: The whole House supports it. 
PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Sir, who is the Railway Board to  do this? Who has 
taken this decision? I simply can't digest it and I  cannot believe that Shri Lalu 
Prasad Yadav will do that. I felt so bad. Some of these people were blind. They 
were weeping and crying. They said they also went to the Defence Minister, Shri 
A.K: Antony this morning. We are staying in the sam e building, he had asked 
them to meet me also. I was stunned. The hon. Minis ter, Mr. Velu, is sitting 
here. Through you, I am asking you to immediately c ancel this. Otherwise, 
come what may, I will sit here on dhama if this is not done. This cannot happen in 
this country. (Interruptions)  
SOME HON. MEMBERS: Sir, we all associate ourselves with what he is 
saying. (Interruptions)  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: All right. You have brought it to the notice of the 
Minister already... (Interruptions)....  
PROF. P.J KURIEN: I am happy, Sir, Laluji is coming. (Interruptions)...

SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, it is my privilege to speak on the Railway 
Budget as a second speaker on behalf of the AIADMK. My colleague, Smt. Gokula 
Indira, has already covered a number of points which I had in my mind to speak for Tamil 
Nadu. However, I hasten to present a few more relevant points which are the felt need of 
Tamil Nadu. 
Coming to point number one, Sir, I have been repeatedly urging to go in for broad gauge 
conversion between Madurai and Bodi. I am very much sorry and disappointed to note that 
the said gauge conversion is not viable, according to Railways. I am one who always urge 
upon the regional imbalance existing in Tamil Nadu in the gauge conversion to be corrected 
and compensated with retrospective effect. To my surprise, now, I am told that gauge 
conversion between Mudurai and Bodi is the only stretch left out. In this connection, may I 
submit for the kind consideration of the hon. Minister and others concerned that the Railways 
should not see a project in terms of commercial outlook i.e. in terms of anna paisa. But, it 
should 
324 

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
be taken and treated as a service organization which should be concerned about the service 
and welfare of the people. Under these circumstances, I request the hon. Minister to treat 
this issue as a special case and see that this gaug e conversion project is 
completed. 
Coming to the next most important point which is universally accepted is the heed of 
having a new Railway line between Dindigul and Sabarimala which is attracting pilgrims 
from various parts of the country. Luckly, the proposal for survey has been accepted 
from Dindigul to Kumily. The remaining stretch in this proposal may also be taken up 
immediately within a timeframe. For information of the hon. Minister, I would like to 
remind him that the survey was taken up earlier and for the reasons known to them, it 
was left out. But, I am sure, this survey, at least, would see the light of the day and 
materialize very soon. Sir, there is a long-pending demand to connect Egmore with the 
Central Railway station to facilitate the passengers. The proposal is already approved 
by the Ministry and foundation stone was already laid. But, till now the project is not taken 
up. I request the hon. Minister of Railways to allocate the necessary funds and 
complete the work without any further delay. 
Sir, the Government officials, police personnel, students are travelling by train all over 
the country. But, they are not provided with special quota. I request the hon. Minister to 
provide special quota for those officials. 
The Railway Budget should have laid particular emphasis and focused on the safety 
and security of the passengers. What has been provided are some measly CCTVs and 
bomb-detection equipment at a few sensitive places, which is highly inadequate. 
There is nothing substantial in this Railway Budget for the farmers and the poor of India. 
The poor have been kept out of this Budget. 
To sum up, the Railway Budget is an all-round disappointment.

MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Now Shri K.E. Esmail will speak in Malayalam. 
*SHRI K.E. ISMAIL (Kerala): Hon'ble Deputy Chairman Sir, when we look at 
the Railway budgets of the last two years, we find that there is a progressive 
leap we can be proud of. I have immense pleasure in  congratulating Hon. 
Minister Shri Lalu Prasadji on this count. Remarkab le progress has been 
achieved in capacity utilisation. Profit has increa sed considerably. Many 
developmental projects have been formulated. The be nefit of this large scale 
development and progress should reach all regions. It is inevitable for 
ensuring social justice in the development of the R ailways. Steps should be 
taken to ensure that social justice which is a conc ept close to the heart of 
Honourable Laluji is not denied to Kerala. 
It is laudable that a Railway Coach factory has bee n sanctioned to Kerala 
and that a bigger amount has been allocated for the  doubling of the route-via 
Kottayam. The amount allocated for the doubling of the line via Alappuzha is 
insufficient. The doubling work should be completed  as per time schedule. 
Allocations should be made to the required level. I n electrification programmes, 
North Kerala has been totally neglected. The benefit of the Konkan Railway will 
be completely available to Kerala only if the Manga lore-Shoranur line is 
electrified. Steps should be taken to complete the electrification of the 
Mangalore-Shoranur line this year. 
Developmental projects should be formulated taking into account the future 
needs. There will be a great increase in freight tr ansportation once the 
Vallarpadom Container Terminal becomes a reality. T he existing lines are 
insufficient to meet these needs. Constructing Idap pally-Guruvayoor line, a 
coastal line, will be a solution to this problem to  some extent. Idappally-
Guruvayoor line should be sanctioned immediately.

[13 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
I welcome the decision to conduct the survey of Tha lasseri-Mysore and 
Nilambur-Nanchancode routes. Here I wish to point out something. Kerala has been 
demanding new lines for decades. Surveys will be announced in Railway Budgets. 
The Survey will start one day and the whole project dies the next day. We have the 
experience of the Sabarimala line. There are not many other pilgrimage centres 
in the world which attract so many people. Every ye ar more than 2.5 crores of 
people visit this pilgrimage centre. Pilgrims come from Andhra Pradesh, 
Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and North India States. There is no transportation facility 
for them. That is precisely why Kerala is emphasizi ng on the need for the 
Sabarimala railway line. For some reasons the Government is not recognising it. 
This should be solved immediately. 
Similarly another long pending demand of Kerala is Thrissur-Kollankode-Pollachi 
line, which is a line that connects the most import ant pilgrim centres in the two 
States. This line connects pilgrim centres like Pal ani, Madurai, Thanjavur, 
Guruvayoor and Sabarimala which attract millions of pilgrims in Kerala and Tamil 
Nadu. The survey of this project should be complete d and the construction 
should start immediately.Travel time will be considerably reduced. I am saying 
this to draw the attention of Shri Velu. Veluji Sir, Kerala is the State, which offers 
the maximum per capita income in terms of railway fares. There are millions of 
Malayalees living outside Kerala. There are Malayalees in all States. All of them 
depend on Railways for their travel. There should be new trains to mitigate the 
journey related miseries of those millions to destinations in Kerala from cities like 
Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Bangalore. 
There are numerous complaints to reduce their trave l related miseries. We 
have demanded to run the Nizamuddin-Thiruvananthapuram Rajdhani Express 
and the Sampark Kranti Express daily. No solution h as been achieved. A new 
train is required between Bangalore and Kerala. There are so many such demands 
which require your urgent attention. 
Before the presentation of this railway budget all Parliament Members from 
Kerala, from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha had met  the Honourable 
Ministers Shri Laluji and Veluji. We had brought to  their notice the urgent needs 
of Kerala. We had also submitted a Memorandum to them. We had also submitted 
our Memorandum to the Hon'ble Prime Minister. We ca nnot move an inch 
without electrifying the Shoranur-

RAJYA SABHA [13 March, 2007] 
Mangalore line. This is a long pending demand. When this line, which constitutes 40% 
of the railway line in Kerala is electrified, travel facilities from Thiruvananthapuram to 
metros like Delhi and Mumbai will improve considerably. The Government is taking no 
action towards this. This has been one of the demands we placed before Honourable 
Laluji before the presentation of the budget. 
Our demand has been Garibrath from Delhi to Kerala. What we got now in the budget is 
Mumbai-Thiruvananthapuram Garib Rath. We are happy about it. We welcome the 
Mumbai-Thiruvananthapuram Garib Rath. But another Garibrath from New Delhi to 
Thiruvananthapuram should be sanctioned immediately. While replying to this debate either 
Shri Lalu Prasad or Shri Velu should respond to this demand. 
Another point is regarding the doubling of lines. It is very important to double the lines 
from Emakulam to Kayamkulam both via Kottayam and Alappuzha. The budgetary 
allocation for this project is merely Rs. 115 crores. This is insufficient. This amount is 
for doubling a length of 165 kilometres of railway line. This is insufficient. Some important 
lines have not been considered. Ernakulam-Kottayam-Kayamkulam route is a sector 
where a lot of difficulties exist. The present decision is to double 26.5 Kilometres out of 
the 44 kilometre line of the Kuruppumthara-Chingavanam route. The remaining route 
should be doubled. Similarly 27-kilometre line has to be completed out of the 307-
kilometre distance of the Shoranur-Mangalore route. This should be addressed to 
urgently. 
It has been a demand by Kerala to introduce two tra ins from 
Thiruvananthapuram to Bangalore and Thiruvananthapuram to Mumbai via Konkan 
railway. We request the Minister to consider this demand. Similarly the frequency of the 
Thiruvananthapuram-Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express should be increased from 2 days a 
week to 4 days a week. The frequency of the Sampark  Kranti Express from 
Thiruvananthapuram to Chandigarh should be increased from the present once a 
week to at least thrice a week. 
The number of passengers in different sectors, name ly
